title: Titanic Sub: Six Warnings They Ignored
alt_titles: Titan: Every Warning Before the Titanic Dive
The Titanic Sub Was Warned Six Times
topic: deep sea submersible ocean, the 2023 Titan submersible implosion
hook: At 10:47 in the morning, more than three thousand metres under the North Atlantic, a submarine sends a text to the ship above. Three words. Dropped two weights. On that ship, people have already heard a bang. Five years earlier, someone had put this in writing. And he was not the only one.

substance.claim: March 2018: a Boeing engineer emailed Rush: high risk of failure at or before 4,000 m.
McCallum emailed: 'In your race to Titanic you are mirroring that famous catch cry: She is unsinkable'.
Dive 80 (15 Jul 2022) loud acoustic event; USCG found it was the carbon fibre delaminating.
Final text 'dropped two wts' at 10:47:27; last ping 10:47:33 at ~3,346 m.

beats.narration: The submarine was called Titan. The company was OceanGate. And for the price of a ticket, it would take you to the most famous shipwreck on Earth. The Titanic. Nearly four thousand metres down. Each dive carried a pilot, a guide, and three paying passengers.

Titan was not built like other deep-diving subs. Its body was a tube of wound carbon fibre, capped at both ends with titanium domes. Its CEO, Stockton Rush, knew that was unusual. In 2021 he said it himself. The carbon fibre and titanium, there's a rule you don't do that. Well, I did.

cards.text: There's a rule you don't do that. Well, I did.

beats.narration: No agency ever certified Titan as safe. It never had to be. It dived in international waters and did not carry passengers from a port. Passengers signed a waiver calling it experimental. One said the waiver mentioned death three times on page one. In 2019, the classification society Lloyd's Register refused to class it.

cards.text: ...could result in physical injury, disability, emotional trauma or death.

beats.narration: The first warning arrives in March 2018. A Boeing engineer who had worked on the preliminary designs analyses the hull, and emails the CEO directly. We think you are at high risk of a significant failure at or before you reach four thousand meters. He attaches a graph. At the four thousand metre line, he has drawn a skull and crossbones.

cards.subject: Titan hull analysis
cards.body: We think you are at high risk of a significant failure at or before you reach 4,000 meters. We do not think you have any safety margin.
cards.highlight: high risk of a significant failure

beats.narration: That same month comes warning number two. Rob McCallum, a deep sea exploration specialist, emails too. He asks the CEO to be very, very conservative. The reply: he is tired of industry players who try to use a safety argument to stop innovation. McCallum writes back once more, and this time he names the ghost. In your race to Titanic, he writes, you are mirroring that famous catch cry. She is unsinkable. OceanGate's lawyers threatened him with legal action.

cards.text: In your race to Titanic you are mirroring that famous catch cry: She is unsinkable.
cards.by: Rob McCallum, email to Stockton Rush, 2018

beats.narration: The third warning comes from inside the company. Its director of marine operations, David Lochridge, writes a safety report. He wants the hull scanned for hidden flaws. He says he is told that cannot be done, the hull is too thick. And the viewport, he warns, is only certified to thirteen hundred metres. A third of the way to Titanic. OceanGate says Lochridge is not an engineer, and that its own testing beats any outside check. It sues him. He sues back. They settle.

Later in 2018, warning four. A group from the submarine industry drafts a letter. Their words: unanimous concern. An experimental approach that could end in outcomes from minor to catastrophic. The letter is never formally sent, but the CEO reads it, and calls the man who organised it. Industry standards, he tells him, are stifling innovation.

cards.text: Unanimous concern regarding the development of TITAN.

beats.narration: Number five does not come from a person. It comes from the hull. The first carbon fibre hull cracks, after fifty dives. A new one is built in 2021. Scale models of the new design implode in a university lab, so the curing method is changed, and the full-size hull passes a pressure test. The titanium rings from the old hull are not replaced. They are reused.

July the fifteenth, 2022. Dive eighty. Warning six. Titan is coming back up from the wreck when the passengers hear a loud bang. The sub's own sensors record it. Afterwards, the hull's strain readings have permanently shifted. Investigators later concluded that bang was the carbon fibre delaminating. Its layers coming apart. Titan keeps diving.
That same year, the CEO told CBS News what he thought about safety. At some point, safety just is pure waste. If you just want to be safe, don't get out of bed.

cards.text: At some point, safety just is pure waste.

beats.narration: June the eighteenth, 2023. Dive eighty-eight. Five people climb inside. Stockton Rush, the CEO, is the pilot. With him, Paul-Henri Nargeolet, a French deep-sea explorer and Titanic expert. Hamish Harding, a British businessman. Shahzada Dawood, and his son, Suleman. The hatch is bolted shut. It can only be opened from the outside.

At 9:18 Titan begins its descent. Every fifteen minutes, a text. Every few seconds, an automatic ping. At about two thousand two hundred metres: all good here. At 10:47, deeper than three thousand three hundred metres: dropped two weights. The last ping arrives six seconds later.
beats.visual: deep sea descent dark blue water

beats.narration: On the ship above, people had heard a loud bang. It was later determined to be the sound of Titan imploding. Death was instant. James Cameron believes they had dropped their weights and were coming up, trying to manage an emergency.

For four days, the world watched a search for survivors. But a US Navy system had already picked up an acoustic signal consistent with an implosion. On June the twenty-second, a robot found the debris. About five hundred metres from the bow of the Titanic.

James Cameron directed the film Titanic, and has dived to the real wreck thirty-three times. He said he was struck by the similarity. Both disasters, he said, seemed preventable. Both were caused by someone ignoring safety warnings from others. In 1912, the warnings were about ice. In 2023, they were emails, a report, a letter, and a bang on dive eighty.

In August 2025, the US Coast Guard published its findings. The word it used was preventable. It pointed to an uncertified carbon fibre hull, a failure to investigate earlier problems, and a culture that suppressed employees' concerns. It concluded the loss of five lives could have been avoided.
Every one of those warnings is on the record. The emails. The report. The letter. The bang. Titan did not fail without warning. It failed after six of them.

description:
Titan imploded on 18 June 2023 on its way to the Titanic. Before that dive, there was a Boeing engineer's email, a specialist's 'she is unsinkable' warning, an internal safety report, an industry letter, a cracked hull, and a bang on dive 80. The US Coast Guard later called it preventable.

Source: Wikipedia, 'Titan submersible implosion', and the sources it cites.
